# Spiritual Translation of the Core Text

---

**¶2**

After the Divine operative power had established the forms and states of the regenerating mind, it descended and fixed its attention upon the external natural mind. It communicated its purpose to the Divine truth governing from celestial good, which set in motion the three progressions of spiritual influx and caused these progressions, which are established [GAP-1] above all elevated states of love, to operate. It extended spiritual influx toward them, breathed the life of the spirit into them, roused them into activity, and purified the natural mind with truths. And the impurities and accumulations from the three containing forms — those of corrupted truth, of falsity from evil, and of perverted love — which had been discharged into the natural mind: these the Divine operative power gathered together and deposited them into the general mass of sensual knowledge that lies within its boundaries and containing structures. For this reason the general body of natural knowledge is adulterated. It has received bitterness and corruption from the washing-out and cleansing of those three containing forms.

---

**¶3**

When the Divine source of all spiritual life arose in its elevation to the inmost celestial state, it released and purified the revolving cycle of knowledges; it washed it clean and loosened all the residual falsity that was within it. It cast this residue down into the great interior mass of sensual knowledge, like [GAP-2] from an elevated state of love. And that impurity — the sediment from the purification of the cycle of knowledges — it precipitated and mingled with the body of natural understanding. The inherent intentionality of that residuum drew it together of itself; the proprial will consolidated the falsities in this way. It rendered them firm and fixed them [GAP-3].

---

**¶4**

Upon this composite selfhood formed from the general body of sensual knowledge there had been stamped the determination of every particular state and every intermediate state, the determination of every full state and every successive state and every completed period of regeneration, the character of all knowledges and all the general dispositions of spiritual life [GAP-4]. It came into existence from these accumulated states and was separated out from their collective power and cast into the general mass of natural understanding. The representations and determinations and appearances and doctrines and intentions of [GAP-5] were sealed upon the very form of that composite selfhood, because it is the sediment of all those states together. Consequently, every particular knowledge that illuminates and every general disposition that revolves through its cycle: to one this selfhood will be its inducement, and to another its confirmation.

---

**¶5**

This composite selfhood was precipitated into the general mass of natural knowledge in the same way that an obscured state might release truth-become-falsity into the midst of sensual understanding. It was wholly constrained through the operation of Divine power and the governance of celestial ministers. It was swept down into the process of reduction and breaking — the state where it had been formed in the original ordering of the mind. And the general body of natural knowledge also received and gestated it [GAP-6] for its own part [GAP-7], being the primary shaping and formative power over it. It shaped this selfhood into an image, this selfhood being transformed beyond any other remnant form within the mass of natural knowledge.

---

**¶6**

This process is comparable to a formative power that might take the fixed determinations of many distinct knowledges and subject them to the fire of self-love, and fuse them [GAP-8: REVIEW — into a single unified] form of selfhood. These innumerable determinations and innumerable configurations [GAP-9: REVIEW — are brought to completion] and constitute a single composite selfhood [GAP-10].

---

**¶7**

This is likewise the case with the composite selfhood formed from the general body of sensual knowledge, which was shaped and formed by the force of concupiscence within it, drawn from the many doctrines and intentions belonging to the residuum of the entire revolving cycle of spiritual states.

---

**¶8**

The primary pattern of this composite selfhood was established to serve three purposes.

---

**¶9**

The first: that the entire revolving cycle of spiritual states might be relieved and purified of the burden of evil within it. In the same way that the tenfold expanse of interior understanding was cleansed and freed from the weight of the three containing forms of corrupted truth, falsity, and perverted love, so likewise was it done to the revolving cycle — that it too might be relieved and purified of the oppressive evil and the impurity within it.

---

**¶10**

The second: that this composite selfhood might serve as a restraint and a confinement upon the revolving cycle of knowledges and the general dispositions bound to it, so that when these attempt to rise into the interior mind, the composite selfhood in the natural mind is found dragging them back as by an unyielding bond, and they are unable to ascend. And when the powers of that revolving cycle take a determination upon some deceptive course, and it enters their intention to descend into the external natural mind, they are unable to descend because of this fixed point of restraint that is fastened to the cycle upon the {GAP-11} of the expanses of interior understanding. This is the one function. However, the other: because of the vigilant celestial guardians appointed over it, the cycle is kept in continual revolution.

---

**¶11**

The third purpose: that the spiritual influx, the truth, and the love that pour forth from the circuit of the general body of sensual knowledge — and the particular streams of understanding that flow upon the surface of the natural mind and discharge into it — and the truths from heaven that descend to the external plane — and the impurities and regenerated states that come down into it — that general body of natural knowledge will be a receptacle and gathering place for all of these.

---

**¶12**

As for all the spiritual force and vitality that descends into the general body of natural knowledge, and the spiritual reception that the composite selfhood draws into itself by its breathing so as to agitate the mass of sensual understanding — [GAP-12] a plenitude and a [GAP-13] arises between its activity [GAP-14] to purify; but the general body of sensual knowledge [GAP-15].

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: After the Living Spirit constructed things and the worlds, he came up and set himself upon this earth. He gave a sign to the King of Glory, who turned the three wheels and caused the wheels that are found [to turn] up above all the mountains; he spread forth the wind to them, he breathed on them, he stirred them up, he washed the earth with the waters. And the waste and the accretion of the three vessels, they of water and of Darkness and of fire, which had been discharged upon the earth, he gathered them and deposited them in the sea that is within the walls and the vessels; because of this sea waters are salty. For they have received salt and bitterness from the washing out and cleansing of the three vessels.

When the Father of Life came, rising in his ascent to the heights, he discharged the wheel of the stars; he washed it out and loosened all the sediment that was in it. He cast it down to this great inner sea like [the stones] of the mountain. And that waste, the sediment of the washing out of the wheel, he cast it down and mixed it in with the sea waters. Its own thought collected it together; and the thought gathered the waste together in this way. It made it fast and fixed it [in the sea]

The sea giant had stamped upon him the seal of the seconds and the hours, the seal of the days and months and years, the impression of the stars and the signs of the zodiac [and the five stars] He came into existence from them and was discharged from their power and cast into the sea. The images and the seals and aspects and doctrines and counsels of [the wheel of the sphere] were sealed upon the body of that giant, because he is the residue of them all. Consequently, each star that will shine, and each sign of the zodiac that will turn: of one he shall be its inducement, and of another its confirmation.

He was discharged into the sea like this, the way a cloud might discharge rainwater into the midst of the sea. They compelled him totally through the action of the power and the helmsmanship of the angels. He was swept down to the mill, the place where he was constructed in the setting up of the universe; and the sea also conceived him [and bore him] for its part [and formed him] it being his chief sculptor and chief craftsman. It sculpted him in a likeness, he being changed more than the other residue of the sea bodies.

This matter is comparable with a craftsman who might take the stamped impressions of many coins and cast them on the fire, and mould them [into a single] image. These thousands of impressions and thousands of shapes [are perfected] and make a single body [from them all]
This is also the case with the sea giant, who too was moulded and sculpted by the power of the lust inside him from many doctrines and counsels that belong to the residue of the wheel of the sphere.
The archetype of the giant was constructed for three things.

The first: That the sphere would be relieved and purified of the burden present in it. In the same way that the ten firmaments were purified and relieved of the burden of the three vessels; so was it also done to the sphere, that it too might be relieved and purified of the burden and the waste inside it.

The second: That he might add a fetter and a prison to the wheel and the signs of the zodiac that are bound to it, so that when they wish to go up above, you can find the sea giant dragging them back as by an iron fetter, and they are unable to go up; and when the powers of the wheel would take a decision on a guileful thing, and it enters their mind to come down to the earth, they are not able to descend because of this stake that is nailed to the wheel upon the [midst] of the firmaments. This is one. However, this other one, because of its sleepless watchers that are set over it, it is turned all the time.

The third thing: That the wind and the water and the fire that gush from the circuit of the sea, and the rivers that flow upon the face of the earth discharging into the sea, and the rainwaters that come to ground, and the waste and rebirth that come down to it; that sea will be a hostel and gathering place for all of these.

As for all the power and the life that comes down to the sea, and in the breath that the sea giant will breathe and draw it into him that he might disturb the sea [there comes a] fullness and a [stirring] becomes between his movement [and his power to] purify; but the sea [is cleansed thereby]

fills.explanation: The King of Glory "turned the three wheels and caused the wheels to turn up above all the mountains" — the gap completes the causative action of setting the wheels in motion, corresponding to the spiritual sense of causing the progressions of influx "to operate."

The sediment cast from the purified wheel into the inner sea is compared to stones falling from a mountain — a standard ancient Near Eastern image for something precipitated from an elevated state (mountain = elevated state of love) into the depths below.

The proprial thought consolidated the waste and fixed it in the sea, which is the general body of sensual knowledge where the sea giant is subsequently described as existing — completing the deposition narrative before ¶4 introduces the giant.

The list of celestial determinations stamped on the sea giant includes hours, days, months, years, fixed stars, and zodiac signs; the standard Manichaean celestial catalogue adds the five planets ("five stars") as a distinct category, completing the full set of cosmic influences sealed upon this composite selfhood.

This directly parallels ¶7's "many doctrines and counsels that belong to the residue of the wheel of the sphere" — the images, seals, doctrines, and counsels all derive from the revolving cycle of spiritual states (the sphere), whose residue constitutes the sea giant.

The sea "conceived" the giant (received and gestated), and the natural completion of the pregnancy metaphor is bearing/bringing forth — the sea received, gestated, and bore this composite selfhood before shaping it as sculptor and craftsman.

The gap bridges from the sea's maternal role (conceiving and bearing) to its artisanal role (sculptor and craftsman), with "formed" serving as the transitional action that introduces the shaping activity elaborated in the next sentence.

The craftsman metaphor describes melting many stamped coins and molding them INTO a single image; "into" is more precise than the editor's "to" for the action of casting/molding material into a unified form, matching the spiritual sense of fusion into a single selfhood.

Confirming the editor's reading: "are perfected" correctly renders the spiritual sense of "brought to completion" — the thousands of impressions reach their final state and constitute a single composite body, using standard Kephalaia vocabulary for completion.

The analogy's conclusion states that the many impressions are perfected and make a single body "from them all" — completing the craftsman metaphor by specifying that the single body derives from the totality of the melted coins/impressions.

The stake nailed to the wheel "upon the midst of the firmaments" positions the restraining point centrally among the expanses of interior understanding, functioning as a pivot that prevents the cycle of knowledges from ascending or descending — "midst" is the most common Kephalaia positional term for this structural location.

The giant's breathing disturbs the sea, and from this agitation "there comes a fullness" — the transitional phrase introduces the result of the disturbance, describing what arises in the sensual mind through the composite selfhood's activity.

Paired with "fullness," a "stirring" describes the agitation produced in the sea by the giant's breathing — the plenitude and the disturbance together constitute the dynamic activity between the giant's movement and the purification of the sensual mind.

The fullness and stirring arise "between his movement and his power to purify" — the gap connects the giant's physical agitation (movement) with his functional capacity (power) to achieve purification of the sea, linking activity to purpose.

The concluding clause states that "the sea is cleansed thereby" — the general body of sensual knowledge is purified through the composite selfhood's breathing and agitation, completing the chapter's account of the sea giant's third purpose as receptacle and site of purification.
